basis: Intellectual disability, microcephaly and developmental delay define the disorder; delayed bone age and puberty alone do not establish lasting skeletal or endocrine damage.
Sex-chromosome anomaly umbrella includes major disorders with gonadal endocrine dysfunction; additional organ abnormalities vary substantially by subtype.
Autoimmune systemic sclerosis with lung and skin fibrosis; esophageal dysfunction affects >50%. Cap excludes systemic vascular involvement.
Hereditary periodic bone pain is localized to the skeleton; no evidence supports additional organ involvement.
Purely psychiatric paraphilic disorder without defining damage to an organ axis.
Occipital epilepsy; visual phenomena, vomiting and eye deviation are seizure manifestations without intrinsic ocular or gastrointestinal damage.
Hereditary motor neuron degeneration; persistent vocal cord paralysis is a characteristic common feature (>30%) causing laryngeal dysfunction.
Intracranial arterial aneurysm is vascular disease; cerebral injury from rupture is a separately diagnosed complication.
Familial cutaneous melanoma predisposition with atypical nevi; ocular melanoma is not established as common intrinsic involvement.
Progressive myoclonus epilepsy with ataxia and cognitive deterioration; all established damaging manifestations are neurologic.
Disorder of the lacrimal apparatus, which belongs to the ocular axis.
Inherited skin blistering with alopecia and nail dystrophy; characteristic dental enamel defects damage teeth, documented in 1/1 annotated patient.
Ataxia, intellectual disability and deafness define the syndrome; strabismus affects 80–99%, and structural scoliosis affects 30–79%.
PTH deficiency; myopathy 80–99%, cataracts and dental enamel defects 30–79%. Provoked seizures and nonimpairing brain calcifications do not establish neurologic damage.
Constitutional platelet disorder with defining neurodevelopmental impairment (6/7); hearing loss and patent ductus arteriosus occur in only 1/7.
Bone fragility defines OI; dentinogenesis imperfecta reported in 1/1. Lung findings may reflect thoracic restriction or separate infections; renal stones are separate disease.
Isolated structural hair disorder; ocular abnormalities are occasional (5–29%), below the involvement threshold.
Disease of the heart or pericardium; no additional organ involvement applies across this umbrella.
CASK-related intellectual disability with developmental and brain abnormalities; nystagmus alone does not establish intrinsic eye damage.
GIST and neuroendocrine paragangliomas define the syndrome; tumor-related cranial nerve paralysis and hearing impairment each occur in 30–79%.
Bladder dysfunction and intestinal hypoperistalsis define MMIHS; cerebral white matter atrophy reported in 1/1 patient. Evidence is limited to a very small series.
Pectus deformity and nail dysplasia define the syndrome; motor delay explicitly resolves during childhood, without established lasting neurologic damage.
Chromosome 3 deletion syndromes commonly cause developmental or intellectual impairment; other congenital organ abnormalities vary with the deleted region.
Acute right ventricular failure from increased pulmonary vascular resistance; pulmonary vessels belong to the cardiovascular axis.
Candida infection directly inflames the esophageal mucosa.
